summary: The note explores home cooking in Puglia, Italy, through visits to family kitchens and bakeries in autumn 2023. It covers signature dishes such as orecchiette con cime di rapa, focaccia barese, tiella, taralli and Pane di Altamura, stressing tradition, family variations and rejection of shortcuts. It closes with the pantry staples (olive oil, tomatoes, cheeses, legumes) that underpin the cuisine.
one_line: A tour of Puglia's family kitchens and bakeries in 2023 showing how heirloom recipes like orecchiette, focaccia, tiella, taralli and Altamura bread preserve local history.
key_facts: Puglia is a southern Italian region whose cuisine is marked by simplicity, seasonality and respect for ingredients.
On September 15, 2023, in Bari, the author met nonna Luisa, a septuagenarian who learned to cook from her mother, who was taught by her own mother.
On October 3, 2023, Massimo and Clara Ruggeri hosted a gathering in Alberobello, known for its trulli houses, where orecchiette con cime di rapa was made with semolina flour and tepid water.
Massimo and Clara Ruggeri debate using anchovies in their cime di rapa sauce, a variant that has caused familial rifts.
On September 27, 2023, Lucia Martino demonstrated Focaccia Barese at her home bakery in Bari Vecchia, using flour, mashed potatoes, tomatoes, olives and local olive oil.
Lucia Martino warns against shortcuts that compromise the authenticity of focaccia.
On October 20, 2023, Giuseppe served tiella pugliese at his seaside family home in Polignano a Mare; the dish of rice, potatoes and mussels is likened to Spanish paella.
Giuseppe says the layered complexity of tiella mirrors Puglia's history, and each family insists its recipe is the true one.
On November 6, 2023, Adriana Costa made taralli in Lecce, flavored with fennel seeds, wine and olive oil; she criticizes industrial versions as pale imitations.
On October 28, 2023, the De Luca family's Forno Antico showed how Pane di Altamura is made; patriarch Antonio praises local duro wheat and slow fermentation.
Altamura bread is recognized for its thick crust and fragrant crumb.
Key Pugliese pantry staples are olive oil, sun-ripened tomatoes, cheeses such as burrata and caciocavallo, and legumes.
